design.title: Ring pooling, actually trained: the place description keeps WHERE in the frame things are (centre / middle ring / edge) instead of one average over the whole frame (re-run of experiment 17, which crashed before training)
design.init_strategy: pretrained:mobilenet_v2 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..17] (torchvision, BSD-3), unchanged from experiment 16
design.eli5: Until now each navigator described a photo by tipping all its little observations into one bag: 'there are flat roofs, some trees, a wide road', without saying where in the picture they were. A new survey changes many of those observations (leaves, shadows, parked cars) but not the layout of the city. Now the navigator keeps three bags: what is right underneath, what is in a ring around that, and what is at the edge. That still works whichever way the drone faces, and it describes the arrangement of the place. Experiment 17 tried exactly this but crashed on a typo before it trained, so this is the first real test.
design.hypothesis: Experiment 17's hypothesis was never tested. Its run died 30 s into training on a NameError in a log line (train.py used N_RINGS and RING_EDGES from model.model without importing them), so the scorer recorded 1e9 and the harness marked it REVERTED; that verdict says nothing about ring pooling. The reasoning stands unchanged on the current champion (exp 16: truedop_2024 mission 0.155, usable 86.75%, false fix 2.25%, abstain 11%; all three training photographs 100% usable / 0% false fix at the same held-out viewpoints, so the remaining loss is purely the survey gap). Every member's place feature is a global average (GAP) of its 14x14 and 7x7 trunk maps: an orderless bag that records WHICH roofs, canopy, road surface and shadows are in the 128 m frame but not WHERE. The bag's contents are what a new survey changes (season, sun angle, cars, construction); the spatial arrangement of blocks and streets around the point under the aircraft is what it preserves, and GAP throws that away. Concentric-ring pooling (separate means over the centre disc, middle annulus and outer ring) is just as invariant to heading about the frame centre as GAP, but keeps radial layout. Expectation: part of the 11% abstentions, which on this design are frames where a member or the 3x3 block splits belief between look-alike places with similar bags of texture, become confident correct fixes. Named risk, stated before the run: ring pooling is less tolerant of translation than GAP. The training lattice is 24 m and eval views stand 11-17 m off it, comparable to the 21 px radius of the centre disc, so the centre ring's content shifts substantially between the nearest training vantage and the eval view. If ring pooling fails, the train_capture_diagnostics separate the two explanations: if the training photographs also lose usable fixes at held-out viewpoints, the cause is viewpoint (translation) sensitivity; if they stay at ~100% while 2024 falls, radial layout is itself survey-specific at this resolution. Builds on the exp 12-16 lineage unchanged and reuses experiment 17's implementation verbatim plus the one missing import; no earlier-era experiment changed the pooling of a pretrained trunk.
